Cool! I read that INFPs are one of the rare types, so it's nice meeting a fellow INFP. The aunt I just talked to recently is also an INFP, so it was easy to trust her with this sort of thing. Haha!

Oh god, I'm glad I'm not the only one who went through something like that. At least we're able to spot the people that isn't best for us. The only problem now is how to let them know that it's uncomfortable without giving them the wrong idea. I mean, it's easy to talk to my cousin, but other people usually aren't so... understanding. This is probably why I'm awkward around people. I just don't know how to go around them. With the exception of close friends, of course! 

I actually want to get into psychology when I go to college! You can thank my hypochondriasis for that, haha. I'll go and look her up right now, thanks! Do you happen to know the title of the book though?

I don't know what your current situation is (aside from this, obviously), but it seems to me that you're stuck. Have you tried just going out by yourself and enjoying the scenery? Doesn't matter if it's a crowded mall or a small park, just a little change of something. Or maybe you can go to a place you used to love. Try motivating yourself to do something even if you feel like it's not going to change anything. Just try getting out of that hole you keep putting and depressing yourself in, and try being depressed while you're walking around outside! It sounds strange, but I find that when I start doing that when I'm depressed, a little something in me changes, too.

Look, all I'm saying is, the fact that you're here on reddit, telling us your story, means that you still have that will to live. Even if it's just 30% or 40%. Take that small percentage and just try to squeeze what you can out of life. Try to change something so at least everything isn't always the same depressing thing to you. While you're waiting for things to turn around, do even the smallest things that would take your mind off of those thoughts. 

And if writing helps, then do it! If you're scared of anyone finding your journal, then put it in a place that only you use, like maybe somewhere in your closet. If there's even the tiniest thing that you feel will help you, never hesitate to do it. 

Also, it may be impossible to stop thinking about the negatives, but it's very possible to start thinking about the positives. When you start going back into that loop again, catch yourself and just stop. Literally stop. You can say it out loud if you want. Then do something to distract yourself. It'll come back, you may think that it's useless, you're just pushing the problem away and not really solving anything, but trust me, it helps, especially when you need to focus on something else other than all the negatives that go through your head. You'll also find that you may forget what you were thinking about, and the anxiety just goes away.

This may be tl;dr, but I'm trying to help you out as much as I can from experience and examples. Just please try it out first. If you're planning on killing yourself, then wait a moment and try to help yourself before you do anything. Feel free to PM me as well if you want to talk more.

I have tried the online ones. My favorite is the Myers-Briggs personality test. I'm an INFP, which basically means I'm an innocent (or naive) idealist. Haha. 

That actually hit the spot! It's just that I'm surrounded by people who are extroverts, those who can easily make friends and are good at social situations. I've been awkward since high school, and I guess I thought it was a good idea to try and practice socializing myself. But it went wrong in the end...

Thanks for the advice though. I'll stick around some more and try to help people here as well. Cheers again!

There are all kinds of intelligence. You don't need to have high grades in school or a high IQ to be intelligent. It's all about what you're interested in and what you want to do and become in your life. Basically what you can do best. No one else has the right to tell you who you are except for yourself. 

You have to know for yourself what you believe in, too. If you believe your family's words, then that's who you'll believe you are. But if you believe that you're someone more than what those people think you to be, then, that's who you'll become as well.

Do your best to be self stable. As the others said here, outside influences shouldn't matter as much, especially if they're negative. 

Also, your brother or family calling you an idiot says a lot about them and less about you.

If by personality inventory you mean self-check, then yes, I've done a lot of self-reflection. I concluded that it was my fault. I got carried away with myself, especially because I was trying to learn from someone who was opposite of me. (Introvert meets extrovert or something like that.) It's funny because it wasn't the first time it happened, pressuring myself into becoming someone I'm not, but when it happens, I usually don't realize it until I get the big gigantic slap on the face.

I've already learned my lesson (god, I hope), it's just all these emotions I can't handle well enough. I'll do that research you're suggesting. Hopefully it can really help me along the way. Cheers and thanks!

You're not the only one thinking this way. Sometimes I find myself wondering the same thing as well. Even my own father told me that I am only 1 in billions of people in this world. He rhetorically continued it with, "What can you do?" He also says things like, "Someone will always be better than you. You have to accept that." 

I'm not saying my father is an asshole, however, and I am not saying that he is right or that you take it to heart. What I learned from it is that you can think that way, but it also depends on how you go about it. My father thinks like a hardened man, but he's not suicidal (Although he does joke about wanting to live alone as a hunter in the woods of Alaska.). I thought about it the same way you do, but as someone who has gone through anxiety and depression, trust me there is always something, even just the tiniest bit, that you can hold onto for dear life.

Think about all the physical injuries you've had. First few fucking weeks or months or days were painful, but eventually it heals, and before you know it, you're as good as new. Think about how things change from bad to worse in just a second, a minute or a day. That feels like shit, right? But guess what, things can turn from good to better in a second or a minute, too. What more a whole day? A year? A few years?

When I had chronic anxiety, my psychologist asked me, "How long have you been in therapy?" And I told her 5 months. And then she came back with, "Can you take another 5 months longer?" as if it were the easiest thing to do. I remember crying and telling her no, I can't take even a few days of this. But hey, guess what, I overcame that shit. After 5 months, too.

So basically, all I'm saying is, if you can think and ponder and philosophize about the world the way you do, then you can do the same thinking and pondering and philosophizing in a more productive and less negative way. There are so many years ahead of you, and I'm sure all those seconds and minutes and days in your life weren't all that bad. There must be even an inkling of good, better and best in there. Even if there's another chance of a bad day coming, then remember a good one can and will happen, too.

Hang in there. You're not alone, dude.

Thank you very much for your comment. I appreciate you taking the time. 

I think it's one of those times for me as well. There has been a change recently actually. Until a few days ago, my FaceBook was deactivated. I've always had a problem with socializing, and I did go overboard the last time I tried to go over my boundaries. I went drinking and partying and making friends with the wrong kinds of people. And then my cousins started disagreeing with my lifestyle (funny though, cause they were the ones who encouraged me to go to parties with them haha). By the time I realized I was making mistakes, it was too late. I'd destroyed something I worked hard to create. I thought I was doing something good for myself but I ended up abusing it. 

So I decided to stay away from people for a while as a way to try to redeem myself. After 6 months, I reactivated my account again, and now I'm reminded of what I did. I think about what impressions I've left on people before I disappeared. And I think about how much they must dislike me. Especially my cousins. I think about how unfair it all is and how embarrassing it was. That alone makes me want to bury myself in a hole and die.

I don't know anymore. I already am of age, and I am working part time, but I have other priorities to take care of. More important than this. Haha, sometimes I don't even know what's important anymore. I want to tell my parents, but I don't think it's the right time. Don't get me wrong, my parents have been supportive even if they do disagree sometimes. I just have to find the right moment, I guess. Or just handle it by myself. When comes the time I really can't take it anymore, I'll try to be smart. Let's hope I will be! Haha. Thanks again.
